images.alt: A Commodore CBM/PET 8032 all-in-one computer with an 80-column monitor built into its case, photographed beside a window
images.caption: The CBM 8032: a 12-inch, 80-column screen built into the same case as the keyboard, the width that separated a business machine from a home one.
images.author: phreakindee

images.alt: A Commodore CBM 8032 computer connected to its disk drive peripherals
images.caption: By 1980 Commodore's PET line had grown a full business keyboard, doubled its memory, and moved from 40 columns to 80.
images.author: Wolfgang Stief from Tittmoning, Germany

images.alt: A Commodore CBM 8032 computer set up with external disk drive and printer peripherals
images.caption: An IEEE-488 bus on the back, borrowed from laboratory instrumentation, connected the 8032 to disk drives and printers for an office's day of file work.
images.author: Oguenther

images.alt: A Commodore CBM 8032-SK computer, a later case revision of the 8032 with a detached keyboard
images.caption: A later 8032 case revision moved the keyboard off the main housing; the screen, memory, and BASIC 4.0 underneath stayed the same.
images.author: Wolfgang Stief from Tittmoning, Germany
